subtopics.title: South Africa's Energy Mix: Thermal and Hydro

questions.question: Thermal stations such as Tutuka, Duvha, Matimba and Medupi are built directly on the coalfields because:
options: Moving electricity along high-voltage lines costs far less than hauling coal by rail, so the coal stays put and the power travels
The coalfields offer the strongest foundations for heavy buildings
Coal cannot legally be transported between provinces
Cities refused planning permission for power stations

questions.question: South Africa generates little true hydro-electricity because:
options: The escarpment is too steep for turbines
Rainfall is low and rivers are seasonal, so reliable falling water is scarce — leaving only stations like Gariep and Vanderkloof plus imports from Cahora Bassa
Hydro-electricity is banned under water legislation
All suitable dams are reserved for irrigation

questions.question: Schemes such as Palmiet, Steenbras and Ingula are described as water batteries because they:
options: Store drinking water for coastal cities
Generate extra energy from tidal movement
Pump water to a high dam with cheap off-peak power and release it through turbines at the evening peak, using more energy than they return
Charge chemical batteries with hydro-power

questions.question: The share of South African electricity generated from coal is approximately:
options: Three in every ten units
Five in every ten units
Ten in every ten units
Eight in every ten units, with the rest shared by Koeberg, hydro, pumped storage and growing renewables

questions.question: The correct order of energy transformations in a coal-fired station is:
options: Chemical to heat to movement to electricity
Heat to chemical to electricity to movement
Movement to heat to chemical to electricity
Electricity to heat to movement to chemical

questions.question: Coal is milled finer than flour before entering the furnace because:
options: Fine coal is lighter to lift to the furnace
Fine particles expose enormous surface area, so the dust ignites instantly and burns out completely
Milling removes all the sulphur from the coal
Lumps of coal would block the smokestacks

questions.question: Transformers raise the voltage to as much as four hundred kilovolts before transmission because:
options: High voltage makes the current safer to touch
The turbines can only spin at high voltage
High voltage slashes the energy lost as heat along hundreds of kilometres of cable, with substations stepping it down near users
Low voltage electricity cannot cross provincial boundaries

questions.question: Matimba and Medupi in the Waterberg use dry cooling because:
options: Dry cooling generates additional electricity
Air cooling makes the stations burn less coal
The Waterberg is too cold for water cooling
The region is bone-dry, so the stations condense their steam with moving air instead of evaporating scarce water

questions.question: Coal's baseload role means that it:
options: Supplies the constant floor of power flowing at midnight and midday alike, keeping ventilators, cold chains and railway signals alive
Generates only during evening peaks
Provides power only to heavy industry
Backs up solar farms on cloudy days only

questions.question: Acid mine drainage remains a cost of coal long after mining stops because:
options: Ash dumps release acid into the wind for decades
Rainwater turned acidic and metal-laden inside abandoned workings trickles toward river systems like the Olifants for generations
Power stations pump acid into rivers to clean their boilers
Coal seams naturally neutralise groundwater

questions.question: Emalahleni belongs in both columns of the coal ledger because:
options: It hosts both a coal mine and a nuclear reactor
It exports coal but refuses to burn it
The town's economy stands on coal wages while its clinics treat the asthma and bronchitis caused by the polluted Highveld airshed
It was renamed after the coal industry closed

questions.question: Load-shedding proved that:
options: South Africa's coal reserves are exhausted
Renewable energy destabilised the national grid
Electricity demand collapsed after 2008
A country rich in coal can still sit in the dark when an ageing fleet is starved of maintenance

subtopics.title: Can Conventional Sources Carry the Future? Nuclear as Case Study

questions.question: Koeberg's essential facts are:
options: Two reactors of roughly one thousand nine hundred megawatts on the coast north of Cape Town, anchoring Western Cape supply since 1984
A single reactor built on the Mpumalanga coalfields in 1994
A hydro-electric station converted to nuclear operation
An experimental reactor that has never supplied the grid

questions.question: The energy density of nuclear fuel is best captured by the comparison that:
options: A tonne of uranium equals a tonne of coal
A fuel pellet smaller than your thumbnail carries about as much energy as a full tonne of coal
Uranium burns twice as hot as coal in the same furnace
One reactor equals two coal stations exactly

questions.question: The disadvantages of nuclear power include:
options: Heavy carbon emissions during everyday operation
Its inability to supply baseload power
The highest capital costs and longest build times of any generation technology, waste needing isolation for thousands of years, and rare but catastrophic accident risk
Total dependence on imported uranium

questions.question: The lesson's verdict on a conventional-only energy strategy is that it is:
options: The safest plan for the next century
Viable if hydro-electricity is tripled
Achievable once Kusile is complete
A clock running down, not a plan — coal's limits are structural and nuclear is slow and costly, so a diversified mix is the defensible strategy

subtopics.title: The Kettle the Size of a Suburb

questions.question: In the kettle picture, a generator is simply:
options: A huge magnet spinning inside coils of copper wire — spin becoming electricity
The furnace where the coal dust burns
The tower that cools the used steam
The mill that grinds the coal to flour

questions.question: The white clouds rolling off the giant curved towers are:
options: Smoke from the burning coal dust
Water vapour from cooling the used steam — the true smoke leaves by the tall thin stacks alongside
Ash being blown clear of the station
Steam escaping from cracked boiler tubes

questions.question: 'A cable is cheaper than a coal train' explains why:
options: Coal exports leave by ship instead of rail
Transformers step the voltage down near towns
The stations sit on the coalfields while high-voltage lines carry the power to distant Gauteng
Power stations are always built beside harbours

questions.question: The one-bag-in-three arithmetic says that:
options: A third of the coal is lost from the conveyor belts
One bag of every three is exported through Richards Bay
Stations must keep three days of coal in reserve
Only about one bag's worth of energy in every three becomes electricity — the other two escape as heat

questions.question: The paid-us drawer of the coal ledger contains:
options: Electricity cheap enough to build an industrial economy, steady baseload, about ninety thousand mining pay cheques, coal towns and Richards Bay export earnings
Only the dividends of electricity utilities
Free electricity for mining towns
The rehabilitation funds of closed mines

questions.question: The cruellest item in the bills drawer is:
options: The rising price of conveyor belts
Acid mine drainage — flooded old workings bleeding acidic, metal-rich water toward rivers for a century after closure
The cost of repainting cooling towers
Import duties on turbine spares

questions.question: Coal's land bill includes:
options: Soil compaction under transmission pylons
Desertification of the Karoo
Opencast pits eating the maize fields of Mpumalanga, with rehabilitation routinely evaded
Flooding of farmland by cooling dams

questions.question: 'Coal raised the house and is now scorching its walls' reminds you that:
options: Coal fires frequently destroy power stations
House prices fall near coal mines
Coal's contribution ended decades ago
A full-credit answer opens both drawers — the genuine payments and the mounting bills together

questions.question: The signboards that end the coal-only road include:
options: An elderly fleet, banks refusing new coal finance, carbon charges looming at foreign borders, water shortages and climate commitments
Coal seams emptying before 2030
A government ban on coal mining
The conversion of Richards Bay to a tourism harbour

questions.question: After the fission stage, Koeberg is 'the giant kettle all over again' because:
options: Uranium is burned in a furnace like coal dust
The heat of splitting atoms raises steam that drives a turbine and generator exactly as in any thermal station
The reactors boil seawater directly into the turbines
Nuclear stations skip the cooling stage entirely

questions.question: South Africa's high-level nuclear waste is held:
options: In sealed shafts under the Drakensberg
At a reprocessing plant in Gauteng
At Koeberg itself and at the Vaalputs disposal site in the Northern Cape
It is shipped abroad every five years

questions.question: The verdict to write at the fork is:
options: Stay on the coal road until the seams run out
Switch entirely to nuclear regardless of cost
Import all future electricity from neighbours
Drive several roads at once — coal is a countdown and nuclear is slow and costly, so the answer is a diversified mix
